description.narrative: The emergency assistance loan will rehabilitate public infrastructure that was damaged by torrential rains and flooding that occurred over the Fiji Islands in January 2009. The rehabilitation includes main and rural roads - it involves stabilization of landslides, resurfacing, reconstruction of culverts, and repairs and improvements to wet crossings. The Project will also rehabilitate agricultural drainage schemes and water supplies. Design and construction will incorporate climate proofing to the extent economically feasible. The Project will be implemented under a sector approach.

The outcome will be the restoration of economic and social activities in affected areas to pre-disaster levels.

Road transport services operate at pre-disaster levels on rehabilitated roads. Progress/Status: Of the five subprojects, four were completed and one expected to complete by Aug 2015. (1) Kings Road (Tavua/Rakiraki) Rehabilitation completed on 23 Aug 2013, (2) Regravelling of Koronivia/Lokida/Toga/Waila completed on 29 Jul 2013, (3) Regravelling of Monasavu/Nadarivatu Roads completed on 26 Oct 2013, (4) Stabilization of Lomaloma Landslip completed on 20 Oct 2014. (5) Construction of Rakiraki Bridge expected to complete by Q3 2015 (August). Data Source: DNR traffic counts. Actual value:
